records.name: InKind Baking Project
records.summary: Volunteer bakers make homemade treats for events and partner groups. Volunteers sign up for baking shifts through a scheduling site, and groups can ask for baked goods.
records.what_you_do: Bake as a volunteer, work a shift, or ask for baked goods for your group.

schedule.text: Baking shifts for events, partner groups and community fridges are posted on a scheduling site. Volunteers pick the shifts that fit their week and can help as often or as rarely as they like.

cost.text: Joining the scheduling site is free and volunteering is unpaid. Volunteers usually cover their own ingredients. The RISE Fund can reimburse up to $25 per event per month, while funds last, if the request is sent before you sign up for an event.

first_step.how: Fill out the Baker Intake Form linked from the Become a Baker page, then accept the scheduling site invite and sign up for a baking shift.
first_step.basis: The Become a Baker page welcomes new bakers and lays out a two step way in: an intake form, then an invite to the scheduling site. A steering committee member reviews each form by hand, so the invite can take a day or two, sometimes longer.
first_step.what_to_expect: Before your first bake, expect a short sign up: the intake form, then an invite to the scheduling site. Bakers can be professionals or people baking at home, and every item must be labeled with its ingredients and allergens and a note that it was prepared in a home kitchen. The pages I could read do not say how long a shift takes, so ask the project before your first one.
first_visit_tips: Watch the info session video on the project's website before you sign up for a shift.
Plan your own drop-off: the project does not arrange transport, though the RISE Fund may help with drop-off costs.
If you cannot make a shift, cancel on the scheduling site and email the project. Within 2 weeks, find a replacement first and give at least 72 hours' notice.
Ask the project where and when to bring the goods, since the pages do not say.

records.notes: Every page I read carries only a 2022 copyright footer, which is not used as evidence. The resources page lists a Baker Info Session video as 2026 with no month, so status stays probably_active and last_sign_of_life is left out. Shift length, where baking happens, what to bring and any background check are not stated on any page I read. The fiscal sponsor is named CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia on the resources page and Culture Trust Philadelphia on the FAQ; the lead entry uses the link tier 1 already had, not checked. The one time October 31 fundraiser was removed from the schedule text.

records.name: Inter Philly FC (formerly Fairmount Soccer Association)
records.summary: A youth soccer club formed by merging Fairmount Soccer Association with two other Philadelphia clubs. It has programs from beginner to competitive play, plus travel tryouts, and the site lists players born 2014 through 2023 as eligible.
records.what_you_do: Players register through the club's online dashboard and join fall or travel teams. The older site lists toddler, intramural and academy programs by age, and Edgely Field is the listed field.

schedule.text: The club runs fall seasons and travel teams, and it announces travel tryouts on its site. Practice days, practice times and season dates are not posted on the pages I could read.

cost.text: Fees, scholarships and free options are not listed on the pages I could read.

first_step.how: Create a Sprocket account, then register through the club dashboard at philadelphiainternationalfc.com. Tryout dates are not posted on the pages I could read, so email the club to ask about the next season.
first_step.basis: The club says its programs run from beginners to competitive players and explains how to register through its dashboard. The pages I could read do not describe the beginner group in detail.
first_step.what_to_expect: Programs are grouped by age: the older site lists a toddler and kids program for ages 2 to 4, an intramural program for ages 5 to 15, and an academy for ages 5 to 7. The listed field is Edgely Field, but the site does not give practice times, season dates or fees. Ask the club which team fits a new player before you register.
first_visit_tips: Make your Sprocket account before you try to register, since the site says one is required.
A Spanish version of the tryout information is on the club's site.

records.notes: The club's new site (philadelphiainternationalfc.com), including its home page and its announcement, FAQ and Spanish tryout pages, returned no readable text to the fetch tool, so tryout dates, fees and the 2026 season are unverified. One web search for fall 2026 registration found nothing confirmed. The newest season on the old site is Fall 2025 with no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out. Krista's address at the club's domain is also published on the old site. Third party directories give other names and a headquarters address; not verified and not used. Philadelphia City FC and United Philly merged into the club, so they are not listed as leads.

records.name: International Ballet Exchange
records.summary: A Philadelphia ballet group that teaches a free 30-week ballet course in neighborhood public schools and stages story ballets for school and community audiences.
records.what_you_do: Attend a performance: the group presents story ballets and student showcases. The 30-week course is for students at participating schools, so students join through their school.

schedule.text: Performances have usually been held in December, with student showcases in the spring. Dates change from year to year, so check the events page.

cost.text: The 30-week course is free for students at participating schools. Some performances have needed tickets, for example $25 each for the 2023 Winter's Dream, and the site does not say where tickets are sold.

first_step.how: Check the events page for the next show, then email christina@internationalballet.org or call 215-849-7950 to ask whether your child's school has the 30-week course.
first_step.basis: Public shows welcome all ages and some need a ticket, but the site does not say how students join the 30-week course or where tickets are sold, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public events are story ballets or student showcases, with casts that mix students and professional dancers. The December Winter's Dream shows ran two performances, at 1 PM and 7 PM, and the 2023 tickets were $25 each with free parking. The 30-week course is free for students at partner schools, and the site lists no prices for anything else.
first_visit_tips: Read the event page for ticket prices, since some shows charged for tickets.
Buy early if you can: a 2021 listing said seating was limited.
Parking was free at the Teatro Esperanza shows listed for 2022 and 2023.

records.notes: The About page says the group was founded in 1998 and names Christina Castro-Tauser as Executive Director. The contact page gives the office ZIP as 19133 with a four digit extension, but the IRS record and a 2024 event listing use 19144, so 19144 is kept. The December 2021 to 2023 listings put Teatro Esperanza at 4261 North 5th Street (ZIP 19140), while the December 2024 listing gives 38 East School House Lane for the same venue name, so the venue address is unresolved and not recorded as a location. The contact name Dominic Salerno comes from tier 1; the contact page names no one, and the About page lists him as Treasurer, while the contact email belongs to Christina. The Spring Showcase was at two partner schools for students and family, so it is not treated as public.

records.name: Delaware Valley Fly Fishers
records.summary: A club for fly anglers and fly tiers from around the Delaware Valley. Members learn casting, fly tying and fishing, go on day and multi-day fishing trips, and take part in conservation and education work.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly meeting as a guest, take a beginner fly fishing or fly tying class, or join to get the newsletter, member classes and trips.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings at 7 pm on the second Thursday at the Churchville Nature Center. There is no December meeting, because a holiday party takes its place. Beginner fly fishing (three sessions) and beginner fly tying (about six weeks) are offered through the club.

cost.text: Dues and class fees are not posted on the club's pages, so email the club for membership information. One 2025 meeting charged non-members $10, and the current guest fee is not posted.

first_step.how: Come to the second Thursday meeting at 7 pm at Churchville Nature Center as a guest, or sign up for the Beginner Fly Fishing or Beginner Fly Tying class.
first_step.basis: The club runs beginner fly fishing and fly tying classes and welcomes guests at its monthly meeting, which has a guest speaker.
first_step.what_to_expect: Monthly meetings include a guest speaker, refreshments and sometimes a raffle, and doors have opened at 6:30 pm. Beginner fly tying runs about six weeks and covers the vise, tools and simple flies, while beginner fly fishing covers gear, knots, fish habitat and first casts. Dues and class fees are not posted, so ask the club before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Plan to arrive by 6:30 pm, when doors have opened for past meetings.
Plan a drive, since the meeting place is in Churchville, outside Philadelphia.
Ask about the guest fee before you go, since one 2025 meeting charged non-members $10.

records.notes: Meetings are held in Churchville, outside Philadelphia. Tier 1 published the club as serving the Delaware Valley, but the orchestrator should confirm the in area test before release, since out_of_area is the alternative verdict. The club's older WordPress site shows a $10 non-member fee for a September 2025 meeting, while the 2026 site says guests are welcome. Dues and class fees are not posted. Fly fishing has no exact interest tag, so river_stewardship and craft_circle from tier 1 are kept. Fly Fishers International is named as the club's affiliation, but no link is given, so it is not listed as a lead. The newsletter PDFs run through October 2026, which supports last_sign_of_life.

records.name: The Irish Society of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that keeps Irish heritage alive through banquets, meetups and other events. Members and friends gather for the calendar of events, including a yearly Christmas party.
records.what_you_do: Attend a calendar event such as a banquet or meetup, or apply for membership through the site.

schedule.text: Most years the group holds a Toast to Saint Patrick in March, a summer happy hour, a fall general meeting, a Christmas party in December and an awards dinner. Events are posted on the group's calendar.

cost.text: Membership is a $100 lifetime fee, paid with the application. Public dinners and happy hours have tickets or a donation at the door, and prices change from year to year. Christmas parties are for members and a guest.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a public event on the calendar, such as the Toast to Saint Patrick or the awards dinner, which were open to the public. To ask about attending as a non-member, or to join, email info@theirishsociety.com.
first_step.basis: Several events are open to the public with a ticket, and membership has a clear application. The site does not say whether non-members can attend general meetings, and new members need a sponsor from a current member.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are mostly dinners, speaker meetings and happy hours, many held at the Ashburner Inn. Public dinners such as the Toast to Saint Patrick and the awards dinner need a ticket, while Christmas parties are for members and one guest. The pages do not say how long events run, so ask before you go.
first_visit_tips: Check the calendar for public events, since the Christmas party is limited to members and a guest.
Email the group before the event to ask whether a non-member can attend.

records.notes: The calendar lists a September 26, 2026 screening, which supports last_sign_of_life 2026-09. The tier 1 value of 2026-10 had no October date I could find on the pages. Two mailing addresses are published: one for membership applications (Constitution Place, Suite 200, ZIP 19106, in care of Joe Cleary) and one on the contact page (in care of PFCU, 12800 Townsend Road, ZIP 19154). Neither is used as a location. Whether non-members can attend general meetings is not stated. The friends page appears to be old, with images from about 2015, and names two partners only by logo link; both are leads with names taken from their links. The About page says the group was conceived in 1974.

records.name: Irvin Kelly Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia foundation for veterans moving back into civilian life. Its housing and career help pages say full details are coming soon, and it takes applications for scholarships for veterans' descendants.
records.what_you_do: Send a request through the contact form on the home page or by email to ask about housing or career help. For a scholarship, you complete the application and send proof of a veteran connection, transcripts and recommendations. The site does not list volunteer roles or events.

cost.text: Fees for help requests and for the scholarship are not stated on the pages I could read.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the home page, or email support@irvinkellyfoundation.org, to ask about housing or career help. For a scholarship, complete the Scholarship Application linked on the scholarships page.
first_step.basis: The housing and career help pages say details are coming soon, so there is no clear way in yet. The scholarship needs a written application with proof of a veteran connection.
first_step.what_to_expect: This is an office that answers requests, not a group that meets. The site says it will respond to contact form messages as soon as possible, and the housing and career pages do not yet list eligibility, steps or cost. For the scholarship, the page asks for an application, proof of service connection, transcripts and recommendations, but it gives no deadline.

records.notes: The housing support and employment support pages say full details are coming soon, and the employment page is marked coming soon, so the records describe the type of help rather than live programs. The scholarship page gives no deadline, no eligibility rules and no submission address; the general support address is used. The About page lists Dr. Dionne Dent White as Chief Operating Officer, but the contact name carried from tier 1 is Dionne Danielle Dent; it is kept, and the orchestrator should confirm. The About page says the foundation supports U.S. Army veterans and their families, while the program pages say transitioning veterans, so the record says veterans. No founding year is shown, and the 2026 copyright footer is not used as evidence.

records.name: Ivy Hill Saints Youth Association
records.summary: A community youth athletic association founded in 1966, according to its site. It fields youth football teams, 12U and 14U in 2025, and posted NESAC schedules for its 12U and 13U teams in September 2025. It is also looking for a cheerleading coordinator.
records.what_you_do: Kids register for a season through the registration page, then join a team. The club also has a volunteer page where people can share their interests, and a page for its open cheerleading coordinator role.

schedule.text: The club runs sports programs in the spring and in the fall and winter, and posts its season calendars online. Practice days and times are not posted on the pages I could read.

cost.text: Standard fees are not stated in the text of the pages I could read.

first_step.how: Email ivyhillsaints2018@gmail.com to ask which fall or winter 2026 program is open, since the registration page's Google form covers the 2025 to 2026 spring season.
first_step.basis: Registration is through a Google form or a paper copy, but the site does not say how tryouts, team placement or new players are handled.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each player is registered on a form, and families may be asked for paperwork such as a birth certificate or a school profile. Once a player is registered, the club places them on a team for its season, and the league calendar is posted on the site. The site does not name a practice field, so ask where to show up before the first practice.
first_visit_tips: If you prefer paper, print the registration form and bring it to the field to fill out before a workout.
Ask which field and practice time apply, since the site does not say.

records.notes: Founding year corrected to 1966: the About page says founded in 1966 and the cheerleading page says Est 1966. The tier 1 summary said 1971, and no page read says 1971. The tier 1 summary also listed 14U in NESAC; the September 2025 NESAC posts cover 12U and 13U, so the summary separates them. A 2026 menu label reading Fall and Winter Sports Programs 2026 has no month and is not used as dated evidence, so status stays probably_active. A page summary mentioned paperwork such as a birth certificate and a school profile; this was not checked line by line on the registration page. Facebook and Instagram links exist, but their addresses were not captured. The volunteer page has a form with no direct link.

notes: All seven batch groups were read and written as publish records. 42 WebFetch calls and 1 WebSearch were used; no 403s or bot checks were met. Changes to tier 1 facts: Ivy Hill founding year is 1966 (two site pages say so), and its 14U NESAC claim was adjusted; Irvin Kelly housing and career pages say coming soon, so its newcomer rating dropped to 2 and the summary was reworded; Irish Society dues, membership sponsor rule and public event pricing are now known, and last_sign_of_life is 2026-09; Inter Philly FC's new site returned no readable text, so its tryout and fee facts remain unverified. Delaware Valley Fly Fishers meets outside Philadelphia and is flagged for the in area check. Contact name conflicts are noted on the Irvin Kelly, International Ballet Exchange and Irish Society records. Not finished in every case: some fields are left out where no page said them.
